en.html:
I woke in an unfamiliar place.

A white, clean-looking room. Not large—six tatami mats at most. Yet there was so little in it that it looked strangely empty.

Only the plain bed I had been lying on until a moment ago possessed any real presence. One chair and a few small objects accounted for the rest.

Looking again, I found not even a window in the walls. No doubt that was why the room felt stifling. There was a vent, but whatever it did for the body, it was nowhere near sufficient for the mind.

My skull, heavy as though packed with lead, demanded that I get out first and consider matters afterward.

I found a door in one corner and walked toward it.

Only a few steps, and I stumbled several times in taking them. For some reason, my hands and feet felt dull.

Somehow I reached it, feeling as though I were moving another person's body by strings. I took the knob, turned it, and pulled.

I woke in an unfamiliar place.

A white, clean-looking room. Not large—six tatami mats at most. Yet there was so little in it that it looked strangely empty.

Only the plain bed I had been lying on until a moment ago possessed any real presence. One chair and a few small objects accounted for the rest.

Looking again, I found not even a window in the walls. No doubt that was why the room felt stifling. There was a vent, but whatever it did for the body, it was nowhere near sufficient for the mind.

My skull, heavy as though packed with lead, demanded that I get out first and consider matters afterward.

I found a door in one corner and walked toward it.

Only a few steps, and I stumbled several times in taking them. For some reason, my hands and feet felt dull.

Somehow I reached it, feeling as though I were moving another person's body by strings. I took the knob, turned it, and pulled.

ja.html:
目覚めたそこは、未知の場所だった。

　白く、清潔感のある部屋だ。
　広くはない。せいぜい六畳だろう。だが物が少ない
せいか、やけに空漠として見える。

　存在感を有する物体は、たった今まで我が身を横た
えていた質素な<ruby>寝台<rt>ベッド</rt></ruby>くらいしかない。
　後は椅子が一つと、小物が数点。

　見直せば、壁に窓すら無かった。
　息苦しさを覚えるのは間違いなくそのせいだろう。
通風孔はあるが、身体的にはともかく心理的には全く
必要充分でない。

　鉛を詰めたように重い頭蓋は、考えを巡らせる前に
まずここから出る事を要求していた。
　
　部屋の一隅に扉を見つけ、そちらに歩く。

　ほんの数歩を進むために、幾度かよろめいた。
　どういうわけか、手足の感覚が鈍い。

　他人の体を糸で操っている心地になりながら、どう
にか辿り着く。
　<ruby>把手<rt>ノブ</rt></ruby>を掴んで、回して引いた。

en.html:
Very well. One new fact had established itself.

The door would not open. It was locked—from the outside, naturally.

I examined every inch around the handle. No keyhole, button or trigger. There was no way to open it.

In short, I was being confined.

...No. Was that not a hasty conclusion?

This might simply be a hospital room. The lock might be to keep unauthorized people out. Certain patients' conditions could require a room which could not be opened from within.

If so, my first duty was simple enough. Inform somebody outside that I was awake.

さて。
　状況が新たに一つ判明した。

　扉は開かない。
　鍵が掛けられている。無論、外側から。

　把手を舐めるように見回してみようが、鍵穴もなけ
ればボタンも引き金もない。
　開ける事は不可能だった。

　つまり監禁されている。

　……いや。
　決め付けるのは早計か。

　ここは単に病院の病室であり、鍵が掛かっているの
は関係者以外の立ち入りを禁ずる為なのかもしれない。
　患者の症状によっては、内側から開けられない部屋
に収容する必要もあるだろう。

　で、あれば――とりあえず、すべきは一つだ。
　起床した事実を外へ伝えよう。

en.html:
That appeared to be the position.

Say I had no idea why, and I would deserve an accusation of amnesia. Not enough time had passed for my memory of opposing GHQ officers on Enoshima to wear away.

Silver Star's arrival had brought that incident to a chaotic close. It did not follow that GHQ had changed its mind and decided to leave me alone. A further move from them was only to be expected.

Even so, this was sudden. That explanation did not quite account for finding myself here with no connecting thread at all.

No... connecting thread?

A connection.

I had been going to Kenchoji to save the Prince and the others...

Yes... the attack on Kenchoji. In other words, that had been————the Occupation's...?

Then that, too—

そういう事になりそうだった。

　理由に心当たりがない…………などと口にしたなら
健忘症の謗りを受けるだろう。
　江ノ島でＧＨＱの将校らと敵対した記憶は、風化さ
せてしまうには流石にまだ時が足りなかった。

　あの折は銀星号の登場によって何もかも混沌の内に

しようと変心したとは思えない。
　次の手を仕掛けて来るのは、むしろ当然とも言えた。

　しかし、それにしても突然である。
　何の脈絡もなくこんな始末になった事の説明として
は充分でない。

　いや……脈絡？

　そうだ……建朝寺への攻撃。
　要するに、あれは――――進駐軍の……？

　では、あれも――

en.html:
.......................................................

Even calling aloud brought no answering ring of metal. Could she not hear me? Or could she hear, but not answer...?

A rare state of affairs. Not in any favorable sense.

A wielder and an armor joined by a bond became one warrior between them. One might call them a single being. For the two to be parted, therefore, was not possible.

Even at a distance where neither could see the other, they could speak as though side by side.

Now we could not.

The most plausible possibility was that she had lost the ability to speak.

Which would mean complete destruction.

The dead had no voice. Even an armor, difficult as it was to classify simply as a living creature, could not escape that saying.

en.html:
—Apart from that, the only possibility I could think of was that she had been sealed inside an isolation box. Whether GHQ would take so much trouble over me, whom it had tried to remove as an obstruction, was very doubtful.

Still... this body was alive, despite the tetrodotoxin that had invaded it. If Muramasa had restored it, she must at least have been intact until that work was complete...

Whatever the case, I was in no position to verify the facts.

I would have to wait for something to happen. My freedom was gone, and I had no means to recover it. That left one choice.

...A thing like that, I did not wish to call a choice.

To do at least the best still available, I returned to the bed and lay down. My body remained heavy with fatigue.
en.text:
—Apart from that, the only possibility I could think of was that she had been sealed inside an isolation box. Whether GHQ would take so much trouble over me, whom it had tried to remove as an obstruction, was very doubtful.

Still... this body was alive, despite the tetrodotoxin that had invaded it. If Muramasa had restored it, she must at least have been intact until that work was complete...

Whatever the case, I was in no position to verify the facts.

I would have to wait for something to happen. My freedom was gone, and I had no means to recover it. That left one choice.

...A thing like that, I did not wish to call a choice.

To do at least the best still available, I returned to the bed and lay down. My body remained heavy with fatigue.

――それ以外には、<ruby>通信遮断装置<rt>アイソレーションボックス</rt></ruby>に密封されている
可能性くらいしか思い当たらないが。
　ＧＨＱが邪魔者として始末しようとした<ruby>村正<rt>おれ</rt></ruby>の為に
そこまでの手間を掛けるものかどうか、大いに疑問だ。

　ただ……<ruby>猛毒<rt>テトロドトキシン</rt></ruby>に冒されたこの肉体が生存している。
　村正が回復させたのだとすれば、少なくともそれが
終了するまでは健在だったという事になる……。

　いずれにしろ、今は事実を確認できる状態にない。

　動きが起こるのを待つしかないだろう。
　自由を奪われ、その自由を取り戻す方法もない以上、
それが唯一の選択だ。

　……そんな事を選択などと呼びたくはないが。
　
　俺はせめてもの最善を尽くすべく、ベッドに戻って
いまだ疲れが濃く残る身体を横たえた。
